text:
Anna Li: Quick ping — I'm putting together a short plan for migrating the model pin/rollout metadata so we can add new fields without breaking older runtimes. thoughts?
Derek M.: Nice. main constraints? backwards-compat with older clients & cheap runtime checks.
Sophia R.: +1. Also need to avoid a large synchronous backfill that stalls control-plane updates.
Anna Li: Exactly. Proposal: introduce a thin 'surface-gating' approach — metadata keys are namespaced and opt-in. New keys live under `meta.v2.*`. Runtimes default to ignoring unknown top-level keys but will honor `meta.v2/flags` once they advertise support.
Mark P.: Can you sketch how runtime advertises support? feature flag or capability header?
Anna Li: Two parts: at deployment time, runtime sets a capability bit in the model manifest (e.g., `capabilities: ["meta_v2"]`). The control plane uses that to decide whether to serve recipes using v2 fields or to synthesize compatible v1 values.
Claire O.: How do we handle mixed fleets? some nodes support meta_v2 and others don't.
Anna Li: Smart routing. Route requests with v2-only rollouts to compatible nodes. For spiky traffic, we can auto-fallback to a v1-compatible variant. We'll encode fallback priorities in the rollout metadata.
Derek M.: What about clients that read metadata? e.g., ingestion/export tools that parse rollout tags.
Sophia R.: We should preserve stable aliases. i.e., keep `pin_id` and `version` at top-level for v1 consumers and duplicate or map newer semantics under `meta.v2` so tools keep working.
Mark P.: Migration mechanics? do we backfill v2 keys everywhere or generate on-read?
Anna Li: Prefer on-read synthesis plus an async backfill. On-read lets us serve immediately without a heavy upgrade step. Backfill jobs will create v2 records gradually and we expose progress via a control-plane job status API.
infra-bot: Deploy-bot: canary started for control-plane backfill job (job_id: cfb-2026-03). 2/20 shards succeeded so far.
Claire O.: Telemetry: add counters for `rollout_v2_applied`, `fallback_to_v1`, and `unknown_meta_ignored` so we can measure compatibility surface.
Derek M.: Important: don't let unknown new fields silently change routing. Must be explicit gate for anything that affects placement or affinity.
Anna Li: Agree. Define a small whitelist of semantic effects that require capability: placement, affinity, cost_hint. Anything else is safe to ignore if unknown.
Sophia R.: For schema, suggest something like:```
{
  "pin_id": "abc123",
  "version": "2026-03-01",
  "meta.v2": {
    "flags": { "prefer_gpu": true },
    "affinity": { "zone": "us-west-2" },
    "placement_policy": "soft"
  }
}
```
Anna Li: Nice. We'll document that runtimes must not fail on unknown keys and must log an `ignored_meta` metric.
Mark P.: How to test? Add a synthetic canary where we deploy a rollout that uses a new v2-only field and only target a small set of nodes with capability. Verify `fallback_to_v1` is never triggered in the canary.
Claire O.: Also include a read-path compatibility test in the SDKs — a parser mode that warns when v2 fields are present but not understood.
Derek M.: Anything for older persisted pins? e.g., export/import between clusters?
Anna Li: We keep export format backwards-compatible by always emitting v1 fields and optionally including `meta.v2`. Importers that understand v2 can opt-in.
Sophia R.: One last thought — add an explicit `schema_version` field on the rollout manifest so we can force strict validation when teams opt in.
Anna Li: Good call. I'll draft a short RFC with: namespacing rules, capability bits, on-read synthesis + async backfill plan, telemetry counters, and the canary test matrix. Will drop a link here when ready. :rocket: 
Mark P.: Thanks — happy to review the RFC.
Claire O.: +1, will help with telemetry dashboard.
Derek M.: Ping me when the canary is scheduled.
Anna Li: Will do. Thanks everyone.
